reps.name: AJ Munoz
reps.headlineGap: Presented only one repair scope with two pricing variants instead of a true 4-6 option menu.
focus: Week 1: Build a 4-6 option good-better-best board for every job
Week 2: Set expectations at the start of every visit with timeline and process
Week 3: Add urgency/value statement before price in options presentation

reps.name: Adrian Muniz
reps.headlineGap: Skips setting visit expectations, never builds a real options ladder, and hands the close to the office on non-repair calls.
focus: Week 1: Build and use a 4-6 option good-better-best sheet on every repair
Week 2: Standardize the opening with intro, purpose, and timeline
Week 3: Close every visit type directly instead of deferring to office

reps.name: Chris Thomas
reps.headlineGap: Under-builds the options menu (1-3 choices instead of 4-6), never offers membership, and leaves visits open-ended when decision-maker is absent.
focus: Week 1: Build a standard 4-6 option good-better-best menu for every diagnosis
Week 2: Add scripted membership offer to the close of every call
Week 3: Lock in specific callback time when decision-maker is absent

reps.name: Corey Reding
reps.headlineGap: When a customer asks about the membership program, confirms their past decline instead of re-pitching it.
focus: Week 1: Convert customer-initiated membership questions into a live re-pitch
Week 2: Structure every estimate as two or more clearly priced options
Week 3: Reduce extended back-and-forth by pivoting faster to the solution

reps.name: J Boothe
reps.headlineGap: No membership conversation on any call, and options are offered passively with immediate decline paths handed to the customer.
focus: Week 1: After presenting any option, ask a direct close-ended question and hold the pause
Week 2: Confirm membership/plan status out loud before signatures on every visit
Week 3: Check job notes/photos before arrival on custom-order jobs

reps.name: Jose Huesca
reps.headlineGap: Strong diagnosis and rapport aren't bookended by a clean opening or confident single-pass price presentation.
focus: Week 1: Confirm final price once before saying it out loud
Week 2: Pair every call with a consistent opening - name, purpose, expectations
Week 3: Convert declined recommendations into scheduled follow-ups

reps.name: Joseph Byrd
reps.headlineGap: Price objections and declines are absorbed passively with no fallback option offered and no firm follow-up commitment secured.
focus: Week 1: When customer objects on price, offer a concrete alternative before moving on
Week 2: Every declined recommendation should end with a specific next action you own
Week 3: Keep all language professional on recorded audio - no profanity

reps.name: Josue Arciga
reps.headlineGap: Membership pitch is not yet a habit - it lands well when made but is skipped on visits that aren't the biggest-ticket repair.
focus: Week 1: Build membership mention into close script for every paid visit
Week 2: After findings, frame what's next with time and cost expectation
Week 3: Capture customer praise with a direct review ask in the moment

reps.name: Juan Bernal
reps.headlineGap: Accepts 'I'll think about it' at face value without a direct ask, smaller alternative, or locked-in follow-up commitment.
focus: Week 1: On every estimate beyond base repair, ask a direct yes/no question
Week 2: If deferred, set a specific day/time to follow up
Week 3: Quote Sierra's price and convenience before deferring to customer's DIY option

reps.name: Kevin Rodriguez
reps.headlineGap: Strong diagnosis undercut by inconsistent execution on sales fundamentals - options and membership skipped on repair call, no verbal recap.
focus: Week 1: Treat options, membership, and spoken close as non-negotiable on every call type
Week 2: When leaving mid-job, give a 30-second summary of findings, cost, and next steps
Week 3: After tiered pricing pitch, ask a direct closing question

reps.name: Mario Conant
reps.headlineGap: When a customer directly asks about the maintenance program, the question goes unaddressed instead of becoming a membership conversation.
focus: Week 1: Treat unprompted membership questions as stop-and-answer moments
Week 2: Every finding flagged during the walk should get a line item in the estimate
Week 3: Verbally restate agreement before starting repair

reps.name: Matthew Arnold
reps.headlineGap: Repeated multi-item upsell pitches on systems with no real issues are creating customer churn risk.
focus: Week 1: Cap add-on recommendations at one clearly-tied-to-diagnosed-issue offer per visit
Week 2: Stop stacking options once customer signals price sensitivity or pushback
Week 3: Eliminate profanity from all customer-adjacent conversation

reps.name: Matthew Graves
reps.headlineGap: Consistently fails to present options or a membership offer even when the diagnosis creates a clear natural opening.
focus: Week 1: State root cause to the customer directly and follow with stated options
Week 2: Make membership offer a standard step on every visit type
Week 3: Close with one-line recap even on short access/staging visits

reps.name: Pedro Manzanares
reps.headlineGap: Skips upfront expectation-setting and stops at 'nothing's broken' instead of offering concrete options to fix the comfort complaint.
focus: Week 1: Open every visit with a stated agenda - scope, time estimate, and process
Week 2: When diagnostic finds no defect, present a menu of options instead of stopping at 'nothing's wrong'
Week 3: Keep phone on silent during active customer visits

reps.name: Stanley Kim
reps.headlineGap: Never resets customer's time expectations, and sales process drags through repeated manager pricing lookups.
focus: Week 1: State clear time estimate at start and update when scope changes
Week 2: Pre-load current repair/replacement pricing before presenting options
Week 3: Replace hedging phrases with clear confirm-or-rule-out statements

reps.name: Tyler Battershell
reps.headlineGap: Loses the sale by fumbling the pricing conversation and improvising steep unstructured discounts instead of closing with structured next steps.
focus: Week 1: Rehearse membership vs. non-membership pricing script until it's automatic
Week 2: Replace impromptu discounting with standard affordability levers
Week 3: When customer wants another quote, secure a specific scheduled follow-up
